chapter: After the Paradise: club dates and Virginia
title: How club dates started at the Elegante; the Town Hill job
summary: Private parties upstairs at the Elegante taught him the format; he then worked seven nights a week at the Town Hill in 1960 and other Long Island jobs.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: How long did you do that on a regular basis?

Well I started doin' it at the Elegante because they'd have private parties upstairs. And I began to see what the format was, if it was a wedding or what, this and that. And we'd do that and we'd come back downstairs and do the regular job out, you see. Then some of the guys were comin' back from the union floor say, "Nick, you should come on down to the union floor, you could make it." Yeah. So that's how I became involved in that.
About how long did that go on as a regular thing?
Well, it was off and on. When I didn't have a steady job I'd do that, you

see. But I would always be on the union floor on Wednesday. Yes. (laughter) Oh boy, oh boy. And then, let's see, I think I'm leaving out another job. Oh, I did a lot of jobs in Brooklyn. I worked the Town Hill. I did that in 1960. Austin Powell, we had the band together. And that was seven days a week, three shows a night, whether it rained or snowed or the sun was shinin'. That was after I left the Elegante. Then I did some other jobs. I did another job jor about 30 weeks...I can't think of the name of this place...and I would go back to the club date field and then I'd get another job, then I'd start workin' in Long Island, workin' in them joints out there. But I could see that things were just goin' down, down, down. So...
